clue.text: Cheese a girl's taken all round a small home

indicators.note: the girl's name is wrapped all the way around the little dwelling, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name; the 's is just the possessive
a cot is a small cottage, a humble little home

explanation.surface: A cheese is carried around a cottage by a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Barred the leftist wanting to join in

indicators.note: the word for join is put inside the word for a leftist

parts.note: a red is a communist or left-winger
to fuse is to join together

explanation.surface: The left-winger was turned away when he wanted to join.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barred' could suggest a pub or a prison, but it is the past tense of turning someone away.
explanation.definitionFit: Barred someone means turned them down, which is what refused means.

clue.text: A person supplying essentials for building new terrace

indicators.note: the letters of terrace are made new by being put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A builder's merchant supplies materials for building a new row of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentials for building' suggests bricks and mortar, but the essentials are food and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer provides food and drink, the basic needs, for an event.

clue.text: The thanks due to a Greek character

parts.note: taken as written
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Gratitude owed to a person from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A worker runs off when such beasts appear

parts.note: an ant is the standard worker insect in crosswords
to elope is to run off secretly to marry

explanation.surface: An employee bolts whenever wild animals come into view.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are swift deer-like animals of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Second given a tip or points

parts.note: a tip is an end, as in the tip of a finger
taken as written
S and E are two compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Someone gets a tip or some points as a second prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a number or a moment, but it is the verb: to second a motion is to support it.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it, and to endorse something is likewise to approve it publicly.

clue.text: Standing to attention before the court

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
Ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Everyone stands up before the court sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at attention holds an upright stance.

clue.text: Shed tears amid function — ham it up

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new arrangement, functioning as fresh letters

explanation.surface: Weeping at a social event is overacting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed tears' and 'function' paint a scene of crying at a party; the letters of TEARS and AMID are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To dramatise is to exaggerate theatrically, as a ham actor overplays.

clue.text: Fulminate against each upset on journey

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word for each upside down

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
to rove is to travel or wander

explanation.surface: Ranting at everyone who gets upset on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove is to scold or rebuke, much as railing against someone does.

clue.text: Quarter people in rented section

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

indicators.note: the word for people goes inside the word for rented

parts.note: let means rented out
men are people

explanation.surface: Housing people in a rented part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter' wants to be a district of a town; it is one of the four compass quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component part, one section of a whole.

clue.text: Those in the very best of health need proper check-up

definitions.text: Those in the very best of health

parts.note: fit can mean suitable or proper, as in fit for purpose
a test is a check-up or examination

explanation.surface: The healthiest people still need a proper medical check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, as in survival of the fittest, it means the ones in peak condition.

clue.text: A single case is no longer enough

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was, as in ex-wife
ample means plenty, enough

explanation.surface: One instance is not sufficient any more.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance or specimen is a single case that illustrates a general rule.

clue.text: Burn a number left in the roadway

indicators.note: the article, number and left-hand letter are placed inside the word for the roadway

parts.note: a street is a roadway
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

explanation.surface: A heap of rubbish left in the road is set alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' is not fire but the Scottish word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England a burn is a small brook, the same as a little stream.

clue.text: Make reparation as agreed

definitions.meaning: to make amends for a wrong

explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to atone; read as two words, at one means in harmony with someone.

clue.text: Note skill's required in this game

parts.note: D is a musical note in the scale
arts are skills, so the plural form is read off the word skill's

explanation.surface: A player observes that skill is needed to win at this pub game.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is the pub game of throwing small pointed missiles at a board.

clue.text: Attack leaders

definitions.meaning: the leading force in an assault
those at the forefront of a movement

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the pointed tip of a weapon, the word is used for the front of an attack and for those who lead any campaign.

clue.text: A top man's pride sent crashing

indicators.note: the two words crash together and are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A leader's pride is sent crashing by a fall from grace.
explanation.definitionFit: A president heads a republic or organisation, holding the highest office.

clue.text: Greensand formation that is a hazard

indicators.note: the word greensand is given a new formation, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock formation of greensand is dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: Greensand is a kind of sandstone, so 'formation' reads as geology, not as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that endangers puts people at risk, which is to be a hazard.

clue.text: Urge going into action when feeling low

indicators.note: the word for urge is placed inside the word for an action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Encouraging someone into action when they are feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is depressed is downcast and unhappy.

clue.text: Suspect made to honour certain promises

parts.note: to dub someone is to honour them with a knighthood
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Someone is suspected of being made to keep promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is questionable or doubtful.

clue.text: Venture quietly to carry on

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to resume is to carry on after a pause

explanation.surface: Daring to proceed without making a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to dare, to take the liberty of doing something.

clue.text: The Spanish will get about ten to applaud

indicators.note: the Spanish article goes round the other letters, about meaning around them

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
X is the Roman numeral for ten
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Spaniards will cheer when a team gets about ten points.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, which is what applauding does.

clue.text: Most preposterous attempt to admit everybody

indicators.note: the word for an attempt lets the word for everybody in, so one is placed inside the other

parts.note: a test is a trial or attempt
all means everybody

explanation.surface: The most ridiculous effort to let everyone in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tall' means hard to believe, as in a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is far-fetched, so the superlative means the most absurd.

clue.text: Outfit for the young, yet in up-to-date style

indicators.note: the word yet is put inside the word for up-to-date

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in the latest news

explanation.surface: A fashionable baby outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the set of clothes and bedding prepared for a newborn baby.

clue.text: In trouble, a real mess, being dim

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words trouble and a real, running across them

explanation.surface: Someone is in trouble and their affairs are a real mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'mess' only completes the surface picture; the letters are found in 'trouBLE A Real'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blear describes eyes or sight that are blurred and dim, as in bleary-eyed.

clue.text: She's a fair target

parts.note: a fair here is a funfair, and the target is the figure people throw things at in a fairground game

explanation.surface: A woman is an attractive mark for admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' suggests a pretty woman, but it is the fairground where a dummy head is the target to be knocked off. Figuratively, the name means a person everyone criticises.
explanation.definitionFit: In the traditional English game a wooden head is set up at fairs for people to throw sticks at.

clue.text: Excited atmosphere surrounding a high-minded individual

indicators.note: the word for atmosphere goes around the abbreviation for a holy person

parts.note: air is the atmosphere
St is the abbreviation for saint, a person of lofty virtue

explanation.surface: An exciting mood around an idealistic person.
explanation.walkthrough: ST, short for saint, is a crossword convention for a good or holy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means stirring with activity or excitement.

clue.text: Not in any doubt about German capital flow

indicators.note: the word for certain wraps around the letter taken from German

parts.note: sure means certain, not in any doubt

indicators.note: the capital letter of a word is its first, so this takes the initial of German

explanation.surface: Confidence about the movement of German money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' suggests Berlin or money; it is just G, inside SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden powerful rush, a strong flow.

clue.text: There can be no let-up for the very rich

indicators.note: the clue says the letters of no let-up can become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The wealthy never get a rest from their troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means lavishly wealthy and luxurious.

clue.text: "Life is real! Life is - - !" or so wrote Longfellow

definitions.text: "Life is real! Life is - - !" or so wrote Longfellow

parts.words: "Life is real! Life is - - !" or so wrote Longfellow
parts.note: a line from Longfellow's A Psalm of Life, with the missing word to be filled in from memory

explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Longfellow's A Psalm of Life: the missing word completes the second exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means serious and sincere, the poem's call to take life solemnly.

clue.text: A poet without any saving grace?

definitions.meaning: Stephen ... was a twentieth-century English poet
someone who has no grace for saving money, who splashes cash about

explanation.walkthrough: 'saving grace' usually means a redeeming feature, but here it is a talent for saving money.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was an English poet, and a free-handed person who never saves is a big spender.

clue.text: Gamble on the centre-right showing spirit

parts.note: spec is short for speculation, a gamble, as in on spec

indicators.note: centre-right asks for only the right-hand part of the word centre, its first letters dropped

explanation.surface: Betting on the centre-right party reveals a certain spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre-right' looks political; here it means the right-hand end of the word centre, TRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost, a spirit of the dead.
